name: add_goal_update
description: Record progress against one of the user's goals. The goal is named by title, not by ID.

goal_title.description: the goal to update, matched by title

note.description: what happened, in the user's own terms

name: add_workout_exercise
description: Add an exercise to the end of a training day. Use search_exercises first to find its slug. It starts at 3×8-12 with 90s rest, which the person can change afterwards.

slug.description: the exercise's slug, as returned by search_exercises

name: ask_coach
description: Ask Khepri's coach a question. The reply is grounded in the user's goals, check-ins, training, and remembered facts, and the exchange is saved to their history like any other conversation.

message.description: what to ask the coach, in the user's voice

name: calculate_macros
description: Work out this person's daily calorie and macro target from the biometrics they have recorded, and save it as their current plan. Use this instead of doing the arithmetic yourself — it uses the same Mifflin-St Jeor calculation as the app, so the number matches what they see. It fails if they have not recorded their weight, height, and date of birth.

goal.description: what they are trying to do with their weight

macro_split.description: how the calories divide between protein, fat, and carbohydrate

name: complete_habit
description: Mark one of the user's habits as done today, naming it as they do. This never creates a habit: if they name something they do not keep, tell them so and point them at the habits section rather than inventing one.

name.description: the habit's name, such as 'read 20 pages'

name: create_check_in
description: Record today's check-in. Writing again on the same day replaces that day's entry rather than adding a second one, so this is safe to call twice.

notes.description: anything else worth telling the coach

name: create_goal
description: Create a new goal for this person. Use it when they have said what they want to work towards and agreed to track it — not to record a passing wish. The title is what they will see in their list, so write it the way they said it.

category.description: a short grouping such as strength, health, or work; optional

motivation.description: why it matters to them; optional

success.description: how they will know they have got there; optional

title.description: what they are working towards, in their own words

name: get_exercise
description: Read one catalog exercise in full: how to perform it, what it needs, and every muscle it trains.

slug.description: the exercise's slug, as returned by search_exercises

name: get_fitness_summary
description: Summarise the user's recent training: sessions logged, total calories, and whether something is in progress right now.

days.description: how many days back to summarise, default 7

name: get_workout_plan
description: Read this person's current training plan: the days, the focus of each, and the exercises on them. Use it before advising on training, so the advice fits the plan they are actually following.

name: knowledge_status
description: Report what Khepri has actually read: document counts by state, how many passages are indexed, which documents have changed since they were last read, and what the last indexing pass did. Use it before concluding the user has not told Khepri something.

name: list_check_ins
description: Return the user's recent daily check-ins, newest first, with mood, energy, wins, challenges, and notes.

limit.description: how many recent check-ins to return, default 7

name: list_goals
description: List the goals this person is currently working towards. Use this before giving advice that assumes what they are training for.

name: log_food
description: Record something the user ate, by name and weight in grams. The name is looked up in the ingredient catalog, so use a plain one such as 'chicken breast' rather than a brand or a recipe.

grams.description: how much they ate, in grams

name: log_sleep
description: Record last night's sleep, in minutes. Writing again for the same night replaces that night's entry rather than adding a second one, so this is safe to call twice.

minutes.description: how long they slept, in minutes; 6 hours is 360

notes.description: anything they said about the night; empty if nothing

quality.description: how well they slept, 1 (worst) to 5 (best); 0 if they did not say

name: log_water
description: Record that the user drank water. Amounts are in millilitres: a glass is about 250, a large bottle about 750. Call this once per drink.

amount_ml.description: how much they drank, in millilitres, between 1 and 5000

name: record_weight
description: Record the user's bodyweight in kilograms. Convert pounds yourself before calling. This updates their current measurement and keeps the previous one as history.

name: remove_workout_exercise
description: Take an exercise off a training day. The previous version of the plan is kept, so this is recoverable, but prefer swapping when they want the work done differently rather than not at all.

exercise.description: the exercise to remove, as it is named in the plan

name: search_documents
description: Search the passages of the user's own notes and uploaded documents. Returns each passage with the document it came from, the heading above it, its line range, and a citable chunk id. Quote the chunk id when using a passage.

query.description: what to look for in the user's own notes and documents

name: search_exercises
description: Find exercises in Khepri's catalog, by name, by the muscle they train, or by the equipment they need. Use this before recommending an exercise, so the muscles you describe are the catalog's and not your own recollection.

inputSchema.description: search terms; all are optional, but give at least one

equipment.description: equipment available, such as 'dumbbell', 'barbell', or 'none' for bodyweight

muscle.description: the muscle group it should train

query.description: part of an exercise name, such as 'squat'

name: search_goals
description: Search the user's goals by text, optionally restricted to those still active. Returns title, category, status, progress, and target date.

active_only.description: restrict to goals still in progress

query.description: case-insensitive text to match against goal titles and motivations; omit to list all

name: search_ingredients
description: Look up foods in Khepri's ingredient database and read their nutrition per 100g. Use this rather than quoting figures from memory, so the numbers match what the person would see if they logged it.

query.description: part of a food's name, such as 'chicken'

name: search_knowledge
description: Search what Khepri has remembered about the user — the durable facts, preferences, and constraints the coach reasons from. Only approved memories are returned.

query.description: text to match; omit to return everything the coach remembers

name: swap_workout_exercise
description: Replace one exercise in this person's training plan with a different one, keeping its sets, reps and rest. Use search_exercises first to find the replacement's slug. Good for when equipment is unavailable, something aggravates an injury, or they simply dislike a movement.

inputSchema.description: which exercise to replace, and with what

exercise.description: the exercise to replace, as it is named in the plan

slug.description: the replacement's slug, as returned by search_exercises

name: todays_nutrition
description: Read what this person has eaten today and the totals so far. Use this before commenting on how their day is going.
